2-derivatives.title: Worked exercises: rules of differentiation
2-derivatives.source: From the Exercise slide (p. 20), applying the rules on p. 19.
2-derivatives.description: The seven problems from the lecture, each solved one step at a time. Try the problem on paper first, then reveal the steps.

steps.note: The power rule, with n = 2.
Bring the exponent down as a factor, then subtract one from it.
The slope of the parabola at any point x.
Constants ride along untouched.
Apply the power rule inside, with n = 3.
Rewrite so the power rule applies.
Any nonzero number to the power 0 is 1.
A line with slope 1 everywhere — which is what y = x is.
A constant does not change as x changes.
No change means zero rate of change. The derivative of any constant is 0.
Rewrite the root as a power so the power rule applies.
Same rule as before — n need not be a whole number.
A negative exponent is a reciprocal: x^(−1/2) = 1/√x.
The derivative is a linear operator: differentiate term by term.
Power rule on each term, constants riding along.
Not the product of the derivatives — each factor takes its turn being differentiated.
Differentiate the first factor.
Differentiate the second factor.
Substitute all four pieces into the rule.
Expand both products.
Check: expanding first gives 12x⁵ − 18x³ + 6x, whose derivative is the same.
